primitives.name: Chronological Evidence Reconstruction
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'time in days since investigation start', 'D': 'document set in narrative chronology', 'S': 'state of narrative coherence'}
primitives.assumptions: Narrative evolution follows a discrete-time Markov process; documents form a partially ordered set under temporal precedence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t → ∞, S converges to a fixed point indicating final narrative consensus or contradiction.

primitives.name: Narrative Coherence Entropy

primitives.assumptions: Each narrative state has an associated probability; entropy quantifies uncertainty in narrative structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When H(S) approaches zero, narrative becomes deterministic and coherent.

layer2.mapping: Entropy-based divergence measure used to detect narrative inconsistencies across document sets.
layer2.telemetry: Change in entropy between successive document clusters.

primitives.assumptions: Documents form a directed acyclic graph (DAG) under temporal and logical causality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Graph traversal fails when cycles or disconnected components emerge, indicating narrative fragmentation.

layer2.mapping: Temporal document DAG traversal mirrors state-space exploration in reinforcement learning.
layer2.telemetry: Path length and branching factor in document dependency graph.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core operators define a structured narrative inference pipeline: chronological reconstruction establishes temporal order, coherence entropy measures internal consistency, and graph traversal enables cross-document reasoning. These primitives form a triadic system where each operator feeds into the next—chronological order provides input to entropy computation, which then informs graph construction. The system exhibits dualities: temporal order vs. logical consistency, and local coherence vs. global structure. Failure modes include temporal inconsistency (when chronology breaks), entropy spikes (indicating narrative conflict), and graph disconnection (when documents lose logical linkage). The operators are mathematically grounded in information theory and graph theory, enabling probabilistic reasoning over narrative states.
